title: Extend regular-locus covers to a proper model

plausible_today: False as stated; characterize the covers unramified at every divisorial/valuative centre instead.
state_of_art: [CL-SA12-030] A complex projective quotient X=(P¹×P¹)/⟨(x,y)↦(−x,−y)⟩ has four isolated quotient singularities. Its regular locus has a connected étale double cover from the complement of the fixed points. Writing the invariant field as C(a,t), a=x², t=y/x, the extension C(x,y)/C(a,t) ramifies at the a-adic valuation. That valuation has a centre on every proper model, so the cover cannot extend étale on any of them. A regular proper rational model has trivial π₁. This independently checked example answers the exact question negatively; it is not a novelty claim.
why_open: The page leaves it as a question; the present review supplies a counterexample and does not claim it was historically unknown.
worth: Worth turning into a precise valuation criterion, because the explicit quotient surface already settles the unrestricted question.
